newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-CAMEROON COMPLETE AFRICA'S WORLD CUP LINE-UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAMEROON COMPLETE AFRICA'S WORLD CUP LINE-UP.

text.p: Cameroon made history at the weekend when they became the first African nation to qualify for three consecutive World Cup finals while South Africa erupted in frenzied celebration as they reached their first.
More than 90,000 deafening fans packed into the 75,000-seat Soccer City stadium in Johannesburg on Saturday to see South Africa book their France '98 berth by beating Congo.
The Bafana Bafana needed just a draw to hold off the threat of Congo, who had to win to make their debut appearance at the finals.

Phil Masinga's 14th minute goal settled it early on for the African champions and the 1-0 victory, in only South Africa's 52nd international since returning to world soccer after almost 30 years of apartheid-enforced isolation, sparked celebrations rivalling the scenes after the rugby union team won the World Cup two years ago.
"It was one of the worst games we've played but all we wanted to do was to qualify," beamed coach Clive Barker after the match.
A brace from Cameroon's Patrick Mboma against Zimbabwe on Sunday propelled the Indomitable Lions into their third straight final and completed the African line-up for France.
Morocco, Nigeria and Tunisia had already secured their places during the last round of qualifiers in June.
Competing with Angola for top place in group three, Cameroon needed a win in Harare to make African soccer history and Mboma's goals proved decisive.
Zimbabwean fullback Edelbert Dinha pulled a late goal back but the victory gave Cameroon a four-point gap at the top of group four after Angola drew 1-1 in Togo.
Morocco and Tunisia ensured they ended with the best results of the qualifiers with respective wins on Sunday.
Two goals before halftime from Noureddine Naybet and Ahmed Bahja saw Morocco through against Gabon in Casablanca while Tunisia got four against Namibia at home in group two.
Nigeria lost their first match of the campaign 1-0 against Guinea in Conakry as coach Philippe Troussier experimented with his starting line-up.

Burkina Faso, who will host next February's African Nations Cup finals ended as the only team to lose all six qualifiers after going down 4-2 at home in Bobo-Dialassou to Kenya on Saturday. They had goalkeeper Ibrahim Diarra sent off after just five minutes for a professional foul.
